blocks.p: Picture a wholesale bakery. Hotels and cafes order every week, and every invoice goes out with a due date.
The cash forecast is a spreadsheet, and it assumes every client pays on that date. But one of the biggest clients pays about six weeks late.

blocks.b: The spreadsheet says you're fine. You're not.

blocks.p: In week six, the staff bonus, payroll and insurance all come due: $188,900 in a single week.
The client's payment hasn't arrived. The spreadsheet counts it as already paid, so nothing warns you.

blocks.b: One late payment becomes a cash gap, and nobody sees it coming.

blocks.p: What if the forecast learned how each client really pays?
That's the idea behind Cash Gap Forecaster, an EXERGY proof of concept. It reads three years of invoices and payments, then draws the next 13 weeks.

blocks.b: You see the gap over a month before it happens.

blocks.text: Uses three years of invoices and payments to learn how each client really pays.
Flags the week cash drops below your minimum: $10,066 under, in week six.
Move one bill two weeks and see the new forecast. Week six goes from $19,934 to $102,934.

blocks.b: A forecast you can check, question and test.
